quiz.q: At its meeting in October 2026, the Monetary Policy Committee raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to:
quiz.e: The 63rd MPC meeting, held from 5 to 7 October 2026, raised the repo rate to 5.50 per cent - the first increase in nearly four years.

quiz.q: What stance did the Monetary Policy Committee adopt in October 2026?
quiz.e: The Committee changed its stance to 'calibrated tightening', having previously held a neutral stance.

quiz.q: Following the October 2026 decision, the Standing Deposit Facility rate stands at:
quiz.e: The SDF rate is set 25 basis points below the repo rate, at 5.25 per cent, while the MSF rate and Bank Rate stand at 5.75 per cent.

quiz.q: Real GDP growth in the first quarter of 2026-27, as estimated by the National Statistical Office, was:
quiz.e: Q1 of 2026-27 recorded 7.8 per cent growth, higher than expected, as noted in the October 2026 monetary policy statement.

quiz.q: In October 2026 the RBI projected GDP growth for 2026-27 at:
quiz.e: The projection for 2026-27 was raised to 7.1 per cent, reflecting strong net exports, government consumption and investment.

quiz.q: India's foreign exchange reserves stood at approximately which level in early October 2026?
quiz.e: Reserves were about USD 734.6 billion as on 2 October 2026, having peaked at about USD 785.7 billion in early September.

quiz.q: The fiscal deficit in the Budget Estimates for 2026-27 was placed at:
quiz.e: The fiscal deficit was estimated at 4.3 per cent of GDP for 2026-27, against 4.4 per cent in the Revised Estimates for 2025-26.

quiz.q: Public capital expenditure in the 2026-27 Budget was raised to:
quiz.e: Public capex was increased to Rs. 12.2 lakh crore for FY 2026-27, from Rs. 11.2 lakh crore in the 2025-26 Budget Estimates.

quiz.q: The debt-to-GDP ratio estimated in the 2026-27 Budget, against which the government has set a glide path, is:
quiz.e: Debt was estimated at 55.6 per cent of GDP for 2026-27, with a target of 50 plus or minus 1 per cent by 2030-31.

quiz.q: The 2026-27 Budget retained the States' vertical share of central taxes at:
quiz.e: On the Sixteenth Finance Commission's recommendation, the vertical devolution share was retained at 41 per cent.
